author: Janis Reeser
title: Former Maryland senator named to Hagerstown Community College board - NewsBreak
text:
By Janis Reeser ,
19 hours ago Andrew A. Serafini has been appointed by Governor Wes Moore to a six-year term on the Hagerstown Community College board of trustees, effective July 1.
Serafini will replace trustee Austin Abraham, who is stepping down after 18 years on the board, including two years as board chair, according to a community announcement.
Serafini served in the Maryland Senate from 2015 to 2020 and in the Maryland House of Delegates from 2008 to 2015. He is a graduate of North Hagerstown High School and Shippensburg University, where he earned a bachelor's degree in business administration. After earning the designation as a certified financial planner, he worked for Van Kampen Merrit and Lincoln Investment Group before starting Serafini Financial Services in 1990. He became senior vice president of Wealth Enhancement Group in 2021 and retired in 2024, after 40 years in financial services.
Serving on the HCC board of trustees, Serafini will act as a voting member of the board in the development and evaluation of college policies. The board functions as the governing body of the college in accordance with Code of Maryland Regulations and oversees the work of the president of the college. The board consists of a chair, vice chairand five members. HCC President Jim Klauber serves as the secretary/treasurer to the board.
To learn more, visit hagerstowncc.edu/about-hcc/president/board .
